root_cause.text: The length validation in rxgk_verify_response() performed the bounds check on the rounded-up token length rather than the original value, allowing an integer overflow during the rounding operation to bypass the length check against the available buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an additional check `if (token_len > len ||` before the existing `xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len` check. The vulnerability occurred because `xdr_round_up(token_len)` could overflow when rounding up a large token_len value, causing the subsequent comparison to pass even when the original token_len exceeded the available length `len`. By checking the unrounded `token_len` directly against `len` first, the patch prevents this overflow-based bypass of the bounds check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in the rxgk_verify_response() function. At line 1117-1119, the code performs: `token_len = ntohl(rhdr.token_len); if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len) goto short_packet;`. The bounds check uses `xdr_round_up(token_len)` instead of the original `token_len` value. This allows an integer overflow during the rounding operation to bypass the length check. For example, if token_len is a large value that rounds up and overflows, the check `xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len` could pass even though the actual available buffer is insufficient for the original token_len. The fix would require checking the original token_len value against the available buffer before performing any rounding operations.
